To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a mutation in the cytoplamic domain of the KirBac3 potassium channel stabilizes an open conformation in a pH-dependent manner and this conformation is stabilized by changes in electrostatic potential at the intersubunt interface.

a mutation in the cytoplamix domain (CTD) of the prokaryotic Kir channel KirBac3 causes an activatory effect that is due, in part, to changes in the CTD that alter the electrostatic environment of the inner cytosolic cavity.

a mutation in the cytoplamisic domain of KirBac channels stabilizes an open channel conformation in which the intersubunit interactions at the cytoplasm interface are altered, and these structural changes are associated with a change in electrostatic potential of a cytoplasmic ion binding site.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the structural basis of Kir channel gating, and our results provide a greater understanding of the role of the cytoplasmically facing interface of the KirBac3 subunits in the regulation of channel activity.
understanding the molecular mechanisms of ion channel gating.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that regulate the gating of inwardly rectifying K+ channels (Kir).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of the CTD of the S205L mutant of KirBac1.1 reveals a novel open state conformation, which is stabilized by an activatory mutation located in the cytosolic domain.
the structure of KirBac 3.1 provides a structural basis for gating in Kir channels.
the intersubunit interaction in the CTD is critical for the control of Kir channel gating.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intersubunit interaction between the CTDs is a major determinant of the energetics of KirBac channel gating.

KirBac channel gating is controlled by the intersubunit interactions between cytoplasmic regions, and this is consistent with a role for the cytoplasmically facing surfaces of the transmembrane helices in the gating process.

KirBac channels provide an excellent system for studying the molecular basis of Kir channel gating, and the results presented here will provide a foundation for further studies of Kir channel gating mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intersubunit interaction in the CTD is important in determining the open conformation of the KirBac3 channel.
we determined the structural changes that occur in the cytoplamix CTD domain of KirBac channels when the channel is in an active conformation.
we have identified a structural mechanism by which a mutation in the CTD of the KirBac3 potassium channel alters the electrostatic potential in the inner cytoplamic cavity of the channel.
